title: Request-level resiliency: GPU memory safety net, KV rollback and smart requeue
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Under mixed workloads with long-context chat and short inference requests, continuous batching plus unbounded KV growth produces transient GPU OOMs. Current mitigations (large-scale eviction and model fallback) are blunt: they either drop too much context or take the whole request offline. We need a request-level safety net that preserves user-visible quality where possible, minimizes failed requests, and avoids bulk evictions that harm tail latency.

This ticket proposes a combined set of per-request techniques: lightweight KV checkpointing (micro-snapshots), on-the-fly KV rollback to a prior checkpoint on OOM, prioritized requeue with adaptive backoff, and a controlled fidelity ladder (context trimming, token-shedding, quantized partial-execution) before escalating to model fallback. The goal is graceful degradation of a single request rather than global eviction or wholesale model fallback.

Scope: implement runtime hooks and admission control changes to support per-request KV snapshots, rollback logic on OOM, a requeue policy that preserves ordering for streaming but allows retrying non-streaming requests, and telemetry to measure success rates and quality regressions. End-to-end integration with routing (to select fallback model variants) and Console metrics will be required for rollout.
proposed_solution: 1) Introduce per-request micro-KV checkpoints at epoch boundaries (cold-start and after N tokens). 2) On OOM/soft-OOM, attempt lightweight rollback to the last checkpoint and resume execution with a reduced batch admission (shrink in-flight batch). 3) If rollback fails, apply a staged fidelity ladder: prefix drop (trim last M tokens), compact KV (lossy compression for low-priority KV entries), then quantized execution path or short-context variant. 4) If all graceful steps fail, perform model fallback to a compatible lower-memory variant and re-run the request. 5) Implement a prioritized requeue: low-latency non-interactive requests are requeued with exponential backoff; streaming requests use graceful partial flush + best-effort retry. 6) Add signals and counters for every step so Console can show per-route OOM-rescue metrics.
technical_notes: Checkpoint size target: < 8KB per request snapshot by storing pointers + light encoded deltas to avoid full KV duplicate
Checkpoint cadence: create on request start and every 256 tokens for long-running chats; configurable per model/profile
Rollback path must avoid double-allocating KV; implement reservation token and ephemeral overlay that can be discarded on rollback
Admission controller change: allow shrinking batch window for requests that hit OOM after rollback attempt; ensure fairness across tenants
Fallback variants: must be bit-identifiable and label-compatible so downstream console can group fallbacks for SLOs
Quality tracking: tie rollback/fidelity steps to evaluation prompt sets to detect regressions after rollout
acceptance_criteria: Runtime can create and discard micro-KV checkpoints without increasing steady-state p50 latency by >5%
When synthetic OOM injected in canary, >90% of requests are successfully rescued by rollback or staged fidelity ladder rather than failing outright
No increase in background eviction rate after enabling on canary hosts
Console dashboard surfaces OOM rescue counts, per-step success rates, and example trace IDs
Automated regression tests simulating mixed short/long workload show tail-failure rate reduced by >=70% versus baseline
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag gated: start on a small canary fleet (5% of runtime nodes) with debug telemetry and request-sampling. 2) Run 48h soak with synthetic mixed workload and real production sampling. 3) Gradually increase to 25% then 100% if metrics pass. 4) If rescue rates fall below target or evictions increase, rollback feature flag and analyze traces. 5) Gradual enable per-customer via Dedicated/Private opt-in before global enablement.
test_plan: Unit tests for checkpoint/rollback and admission shrink; integration tests with injected OOM mid-execution; load test with mixed workloads (60% short, 40% long) measuring tail-failure rates; A/B against control to validate latency/regression thresholds. Create synthetic scenario that triggers rollback path deterministically to validate observable counters.
comments: 2026-02-19 - Ava Martinez: Initial writeup and spike notes attached. Proposed checkpoint encoding uses delta pointers rather than full KV clones to save memory.

2026-02-25 - Rahul Singh: Spike completed. Prototype rollback overlay implemented; reservation tokens prevent double alloc. Observed ~3% p95 latency increase on heavy context paths — need to optimize checkpoint cadence.

2026-03-01 - Lina Chen (SRE): Can we expose a per-host reserve pool for immediate rollback recovery? Concern that rollback itself may trigger transient OOM when copying deltas. Suggested overlay-copy-on-write to avoid extra allocations.
2026-03-05 - Rahul Singh: Implemented overlay copy-on-write and throttled checkpoint creation to 1/256 tokens. Re-run load test: p95 overhead reduced to 0.9%. Adding admission shrink logic next.
2026-03-10 - PM review (Marco Ortega): Ensure Console product owners get event hooks (oom_rescue_step) for billing/SLAs. Also requested a feature flag per-customer for Dedicated.

2026-03-12 - Design (Sofia Ruiz): UX note: when a streaming chat partially degrades, user-visible indicator should say 'context truncated to preserve responsiveness' — design will provide toast copy and fallback UX spec.

2026-03-14 - Rahul Singh: In-progress: admission shrink merged behind flag (runtime PR 4848). Next: staged fidelity ladder (prefix drop + compact) and model-fallback integration. Planning canary rollout next week.
